subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This choice creates a public config/security boundary and can change how existing announce-mode cron jobs use the `message` tool, so automation should not choose the product contract by itself.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus upgrade-safe docs and tests.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions as well, reducing config surface but coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep Per-Job Only
options.body: Avoid a new global cron policy and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus upgrade-safe docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history signal on the scoped capability/tool-policy pipeline and prior review context for this issue.
